analysis.title: GS MORNING: 1) CPI Preview, 2) G10 Spot Colour, 3) USDCNH Fixing Trend and 4) Equities Update (10 Nov 2026)
key_insights: GS US Economics (Mericle) expects October core CPI +0.16% m/m vs +0.2% consensus, and headline +0.21% vs +0.3% consensus, reflecting higher food and energy prices. The forecast is consistent with a larger 0.23% rise in October core PCE.

Mericle's CPI component calls: airfares unchanged m/m, medical services -0.1% (health insurance prices -2.5% as the BLS incorporates updated premium source data), and slower autos inflation (used cars -1.5%, new cars +0.1%, auto insurance -0.3%).
Mericle expects core CPI of about +0.1% m/m in November and December, citing slowing shelter, shrinking tariff-related contributions and continued downward pressure from health insurance.

G10 FX spot desk (Brauten-Smith) says natural USD buying tied to hyperscaler Eurobond issuance appears to be behind us. Yesterday had no indiscriminate USD bid, and G10 FX began to acknowledge the past week's energy moves.
Participation in G10 FX remains light. The desk expects low volumes unless today's US CPI m/m reading is decisive. Tomorrow is a US holiday (stocks open, bonds closed, no USD currency settlement).
The G10 FX desk is tilting its books toward a weaker USD versus JPY and GBP, from tactical USD length versus EUR last week.

GBP longs are favoured over EUR because the UK does not include France. The desk sees 'playing a French deterioration' as probably the second-ranked 2027 trade idea so far, behind short USDJPY/XXXJPY. The desk owns mid-December 1.3700 GBPUSD calls with a cash overlay.

AUDNZD is -1.6% on the month, consistent with November seasonality for a lower cross. The desk cites the RBNZ's end-October hold versus +24bps priced and weaker NZ employment data. NZ elections trimmed the left tail on NZD.

GS EM Strategy (Rastogi) believes the CNH appreciation trend remains intact after last week's FX reserve ratio hike. It favours adding to short USDCNH once the spot-to-fixing gap narrows back to 200-300 pips.

GS EM Strategy expects stronger-than-usual December exporter repatriation and sees USDCNH grinding lower toward 6.55-6.57 by end-January. The YTD fixing's maximum deviation from the trend line is about 0.4%, and the August episode peaked at 0.38%.

Privorotsky (EMEA Flow Intermediation) says Monday brought a strong recovery, with tech higher, Nvidia weakness compartmentalised, and energy sharply lower. GS prime book saw one of the most aggressive net and gross de-risking episodes of the past decade.

Privorotsky says an in-line or softer CPI would challenge the ~80% market probability of a December Fed hike (or the risk of a March hike). He flags hot CPI and renewed Middle East escalation into the weekend as the obvious risks, and notes vol tends to be autocorrelated after a violent rally.

Tech: the first neocloud reports post-midterms today. The question is whether contracted capacity earns attractive returns after financing costs, delays and depreciation. The market is treating Nvidia's company-specific headlines (leadership uncertainty) separately from the wider AI complex.

Data centres: the bipartisan permitting bill cleared its first Senate procedural vote 73-25 and is not final, with the House seen as the bigger obstacle. Privorotsky expects data centres to be built with more conditions, not a nationwide moratorium. CEG rose 10% on stronger numbers, higher guidance and additional generation agreements.

Privorotsky says positioning and sentiment remain defensive. If CPI gives bonds a reason to rally, he sees a move from short covering to a sustained re-grossing cycle (steeper curve, growth recovery, high beta and momentum regaining leadership). He names aerospace, transports, select discretionary and high-quality unlevered AI as areas to chase.
Privorotsky's medium to long-term concern on AI is potential compute oversupply or efficiency gains, not undersupply.

market_movers.rationale: Shares rose about 10% on stronger numbers, higher guidance and additional generation agreements, which Privorotsky says shows the physical data-centre buildout continues.
Company-specific headlines tied to leadership uncertainty weighed on the stock, but the market did not sell the wider AI complex.

sector_views.rationale: Named by Privorotsky as natural areas to chase for a year-end re-grossing if energy and inflation align, given defensive positioning.
Named as a natural area to chase. The market's ability to compartmentalise Nvidia headlines is read as a positive signal.
Permitting reform benefits infrastructure and well-capitalised developers. The likely outcome is buildout with conditions, not a moratorium.

earnings_insights: CEG rose about 10% on 11/10 after reporting stronger numbers, higher guidance and additional generation agreements. No EPS or revenue figures are given in the note.

The first of the neoclouds to report post-midterms reports 11/10. The note frames the question as returns on contracted capacity after financing costs, delays and depreciation, and does not name the company.

Consensus benchmark that GS expects the print to undershoot.
Below the +0.3% consensus. Higher food and energy prices are the stated drivers.
The GS core CPI forecast is consistent with this larger core PCE increase.

trade_ideas.description: Long GBPUSD via mid-December 1.3700 calls with a cash overlay; long GBP versus EUR
trade_ideas.rationale: GBPUSD has a smaller natural offer and should be high-beta on a USD sell-off, and the UK does not include France.

trade_ideas.description: Short USDCNH, adding once the spot-to-fixing gap narrows to 200-300 pips, targeting 6.55-6.57 by end-January
trade_ideas.rationale: The CNH appreciation trend remains intact after the FX reserve ratio hike, and December exporter repatriation is expected to be stronger than usual.
November seasonality for a lower cross, the cross is already -1.6% on the month, and the RBNZ held against +24bps priced.

trade_ideas.description: Re-grossing trade into year-end: steeper curve, growth recovery, high beta and momentum leadership; chase aerospace, transports, select discretionary and high-quality unlevered AI
trade_ideas.rationale: Positioning is defensive, and if CPI lets bonds rally, short covering could become sustained re-grossing.

risk_factors: A hot CPI print would challenge the constructive setup and keep the ~80% December Fed hike probability in place.
Renewed Middle East escalation into the weekend.
Vol tends to be autocorrelated after a violent rally off the lows.
Light G10 FX participation and a US holiday tomorrow (bonds closed, no USD currency settlement) could produce erratic moves.
Medium to long-term risk of compute oversupply or efficiency gains in AI.
House passage of the data-centre permitting bill is uncertain.
Neocloud returns after financing costs, delays and depreciation.
vol_and_positioning: Privorotsky says GS's US prime book just saw one of the most aggressive episodes of net and gross de-risking in the past decade.
Positioning and sentiment remain 'shell shocked and diminished' despite supportive impulses from energy, rates and credit. Vol tends to be autocorrelated after the violent rally off the lows.
The G10 FX desk owns mid-December GBPUSD 1.3700 calls with a cash overlay, and is tilting books toward a weaker USD versus JPY and GBP.
G10 FX participation is light, with discretionary investors under performance strain. Low volumes are expected unless CPI is decisive.
geopolitical: Privorotsky describes a Middle East that is at least not escalating, with enough barrels to balance the physical market. Renewed escalation into the weekend is flagged as a risk.
The NZ election result kept incumbents as the base of a coalition with no dual mandate, trimming the left tail on NZD.
The G10 FX desk notes appetite exists to press the French fiscal trade, as seen in late September and early October price action.

The bipartisan data-centre permitting bill cleared its first Senate procedural hurdle 73-25, and the House is seen as the bigger obstacle. Privorotsky reads the midterm elections as favouring buildout with conditions.

tension_points.bull_case: An in-line or softer October CPI (GS expects core +0.16% vs +0.2% consensus) would challenge the ~80% December hike probability and let bonds rally, starting a sustained re-grossing cycle.
tension_points.bear_case: A hot CPI print and renewed Middle East escalation into the weekend would hit a market where vol tends to be autocorrelated after a violent rally.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A hot October CPI print, or renewed Middle East escalation into the weekend.

tension_points.bull_case: Undersupply is not the problem, and the market's ability to compartmentalise Nvidia's headlines is a positive signal for the broader AI complex.
tension_points.bear_case: Fear of potential compute oversupply or efficiency gains is the medium to long-term worry, and neocloud returns after financing costs, delays and depreciation are unproven.
